articles.title: Brazil bans online betting
articles.content_excerpt: The impasse is over. After days of uncertainty over what Brazil should do about online betting, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government announced Friday in São Paulo that sports betting houses will be shut down nationwide. Online casinos, including gambling games such as Tigrinho , are banned as well. The bans on bets and online casinos took effect immediately. Lula is also expected to send Congress a bill establishing penalties for anyone who operates, runs, or promotes betting. The move came through a decree signed by Lula, which took effect right away. Finance Minister Dario Durigan made the announcement and explained the reasoning. “Our decision stems from the harmful effect that bets have had in Brazil,” Durigan said. articles.title: “Cruel & Torturous”: Christa Pike in Critical Condition After Botched Tennessee Execution
articles.content_excerpt: Tennessee’s Governor Bill Lee has halted executions for the remainder of the year after a death row prisoner survived two lethal injections on Wednesday. According to her lawyers, Christa Pike was still breathing after she was strapped to a gurney and injected with two syringes of pentobarbital in a botched execution that spanned more than two hours. Prior to the scheduled execution, Pike and her lawyers argued a single-dose lethal injection could be tantamount to torture due to Pike’s small veins. Pike was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder she committed when she was 18. articles.content_excerpt: Since Sunday , September 27, residents of Garvaghy Road in Portadown have prevented the Orange Order’s Drumcree march from passing through their community. Linking arms, locals and supporters warned that the parade could undo years of progress against sectarian violence in the north of Ireland. More than 4,000 people signed petitions opposing the march, yet authorities formally allowed it to move ahead. First, the Parades Commission approved a limited procession. Then, the Court of Appeal lifted an injunction imposed by the High Court, paving the way for the march attempt on Sunday.
